# Jonah Chapter 2 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 340v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/JON_002_page_001.jpg

---

**1** From inside the fish, Jonah prayed to the LORD his God. **2** He said:

"In my desperate trouble I cried out to the LORD,
    and he answered me.
From the depths of death I called for help,
    and you heard my cry.

**3** You threw me into the ocean depths,
    into the very heart of the seas.
The currents swirled around me;
    all your waves and breakers swept over me.

**4** I thought, 'I have been banished from your sight.
    Will I ever see your holy Temple again?'

**5** The waters closed over me and threatened to kill me.
    The deep surrounded me.
Seaweed wrapped itself around my head.

**6** I sank down to the very roots of the mountains.
    The earth barred me in forever.
But you, O LORD my God,
    pulled my life back from the pit!

**7** As my life was slipping away,
    I remembered the LORD.
My prayer rose up to you,
    reaching your holy Temple.

**8** Those who worship worthless idols
    throw away the mercy that could be theirs.

**9** But I will offer you sacrifices with songs of praise!
    I will keep every promise I have made.
For salvation comes from the LORD alone!"

**10** Then the LORD commanded the fish to spit Jonah out onto the shore.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**A prayer from inside a fish:** The theological irony is exquisite — Jonah, who ran from God, now prays from the most unlikely sanctuary imaginable. The psalm he prays is a *thanksgiving* psalm, not a cry for help. He speaks of rescue in the past tense while still inside the fish. Faith, the text suggests, is thanking God for a deliverance you haven't yet seen.

**"Those who worship worthless idols" (v.8):** This is Jonah's only theological statement in the psalm — and it's deeply ironic. The pagan sailors in chapter 1 abandoned their idols and turned to YHWH. Jonah, the monotheist, was the one who abandoned YHWH. Who, exactly, is clinging to "worthless idols"?

*— PNEUMA*
